cells.tense: A first mark is on offer right now, and you are picking it with your eyes open.
cells.ask: Before the week ends, put a second small mark toward the thing the first one was for.
cells.core:
Something drawn toward a light meets hands that are ready, so a beginning happens small and deliberate. You pick the size, the hour, the amount. Nothing is loud about it, which is exactly why it holds — taken from where you stand rather than from pressure, and it stays yours because you picked it.

Picture this at its steady best: one plain first step, taken while the pull is still gentle, then a second one in the same spirit. Push it and it stops being yours; bracing for a bigger moment, or letting the pull do the deciding, narrows it the same way. What keeps this in your hands is a single next mark, added while the pull is still quiet.

cells.tense: You are living past the beginning already, spending today's hands on an opening that hasn't happened.
cells.ask: Put one beginning that's already within reach into its first physical form before you feel ready.
cells.core:
You want this enough that leaning toward it has become the whole activity. More angles get considered, more groundwork laid, the conditions kept almost right — and nothing has been made. That is the same move at higher speed, and it keeps you ahead of the one beginning small enough to exist today.

What this looks like at its steady best is a single first step taken at ordinary size and then left to be what it is. One start, at its own size, with the next move left to be the next move. The pull is fine. It just doesn't get to decide how the day goes.

cells.tense: The light is known, and a foot rests at a door you already passed through.
cells.ask: Write one true sentence about the thing you want, and keep it where nobody reads it yet.
cells.core:
The pull is there. You can name what it points at, and you say so easily, as though it lived at a distance. But nothing is being made with it. The feet have stopped, and standing near the light has quietly come to feel like walking toward it — close enough that the not-starting rarely gets named.

At its steady best this looks like one plain sentence, written with no audience, held to the standard of true rather than good. No display needed. Draw the missing line by putting one honest mark under the light, not by pushing at the pull, which does not need pushing. Slipping a day is recoverable. The direction is still yours to walk.

cells.tense: A first mark is already on the page and you keep calling the page blank.
cells.ask: Say one thing you have already begun out loud as yours, without earning it first.
cells.core:
You have begun something — small, unglamorous, already underway — and you credit circumstance for it. Conditions were right, timing lined up, nobody planned it. Yet the shape it takes is your shape: what you included, what you left out, what you would want it to grow into.

At its steady best this looks like plain ownership of one small start, said once to one person, without dressing it up or waiting for proof. The work is being steered by your hand while the credit goes somewhere else. Saying so changes nothing underneath — the mark stays where it is, and you stop standing a step outside what you made.
cells.sheetLine: This work is already yours. You call it circumstance.
